String:
Acre: An Amazon tributary splits the teams
in the far west of Brazil; its fords are the
only ways across, and holding them wins the
game. The rainforest is dense, so wood never
runs out. There is no gold: Brazil's
greatest rubber producer pays its coin in
rubber trees. Tapirs are the main food, and
the river's fish a second source.

An Amazon tributary splits the teams in the far west of Brazil; its fords are the only ways across, and holding them wins the game. The rainforest is dense, so wood never runs out. There is no gold: Brazil's greatest rubber producer pays its coin in rubber trees. Tapirs are the main food, and the river's fish a second source.

Teams start on opposite banks of the Amazon, deep in the rain forest. The river has no fords, so ships carry the war across it, but towers and cannon on the shore punish fleets that come too close.

Teams start at opposite ends of a dry peninsula broken by cliffs, with sea on two sides. A trade route crosses the land and the Order of Christ can be allied. Galleys patrol the coast and can damage ships, so fishing fleets need an escort.

Appalachians: Teams start on either side of
one or two long ridges, crossed only at a
few gaps: a defensive map, where you guard
or wall the gaps and fight for the valleys.
Each game draws one or two trade routes, up
to two native nations and one of four skins.

Players share a narrow strip of land between the sea and the impassable cliffs of the Andes. The north is dry and rich in copper, the centre is grassland and the south hides treasures. A trade route crosses the land, and the rich sea rewards an early dock.
